title: Inquiry clears police in death of gang leader: Officers followed proper procedure in gunfight: judge
article: Police did nothing wrong when they shot to death gang leader Long Duy (Crazy Jimmy) Hoang after he fired at them with a pistol, a judge has concluded.
"I can find no evidence that the police followed anything other than proper procedure," assistant chief provincial court Judge Peter Caffaro wrote in a fatality inquiry report released Wednesday.

"The confrontation initiated by Mr. Long Duy Hoang was short and sharp. Given the circumstances, the police are to be commended for keeping loss of life to a minimum and for immediate CPR efforts to revive (him)."
On Jan. 5, 2000, tactical team members chased Hoang through the west end for 14 blocks at speeds of up to 100 km/h following a failed attempt to stop him as they checked out a gun complaint.
He lost control on an icy road and crashed his Honda Accord into a Jeep at 149th Street and 89th Avenue.
Passenger Hoa "Ken" Tran jumped out of the vehicle to surrender, but Hoang, who had been smoking crack cocaine, grabbed a .45- calibre Glock handgun.
He fired at least once from the driver's seat toward an officer who was ordering him to put up his hands.
The officer and two colleagues fired 30 rounds from automatic weapons into the car, riddling the windshield with holes and blowing out the back window.
The 28-year-old leader of the Crazy Jimmies died in hospital 36 hours later.

Hoang, who left a sports bag containing a loaded machine-gun in the basement of Tran's home on 155th Street, had been losing his grip on his drug and extortion gang because he was using too much cocaine.
Tran later told investigators his longtime friend was afraid of being arrested.
Caffaro concluded the incident was inevitable.
"From the statement of Ken Tran, it seems that the accused did not want to be arrested for outstanding warrants and was prepared to engage the police in an armed confrontation, whatever the cost."
The judge did not recommend handling similar situations differently in the future.
Police spokesman Dean Parthenis said the force is pleased with the judge's findings.
"It's apparent that the justice system approves of police actions in a very difficult, dangerous situation."
